title: Personal Pronouns in the Accusative
summary: Using mich, dich, ihn, sie, es, uns, euch, sie/Sie as direct objects.
whyItMatters: Accusative pronouns prevent repetition when a person or thing is already known. They answer whom or what an action directly affects: the doctor examines me, I call him, or we clean it.

mentalModel.title: Replace a known direct object
mentalModel.content: Start with the full noun, identify the direct object, and replace it with the matching accusative pronoun.

mentalModel.title: Only some forms visibly change
mentalModel.content: The clearest changes are ich to mich, du to dich, and er to ihn; several other forms look like the nominative.

mentalModel.title: Keep subject and object roles separate
mentalModel.content: In 'Sie sieht ihn', 'sie' performs the action and 'ihn' receives it.

ruleBlocks.title: Replace an established noun
ruleBlocks.content: Use a pronoun after the person or thing is clear: 'Wo ist der Arzt? Ich rufe ihn an.'

ruleBlocks.title: Choose the accusative form
ruleBlocks.content: Use mich, dich, ihn, sie, es, uns, euch, sie, and formal Sie according to the noun or person replaced.

ruleBlocks.title: Place short pronouns near the verb
ruleBlocks.content: In a simple sentence, the accusative pronoun normally follows the conjugated verb: 'Ich sehe ihn heute.'

ruleBlocks.title: Capitalize formal Sie
ruleBlocks.content: Formal accusative 'Sie' remains capitalized: 'Ich rufe Sie morgen an.'

sentenceStructure: The subject performs the action; the accusative pronoun receives it.
Short pronouns usually appear early in the middle field.
A separable prefix still closes the clause: 'Ich rufe ihn an.'
Formal 'Sie' is capitalized in every case.

concepts: manage pronoun order in longer sentences
use pronouns fluently across clause types

comparisons.summary: The accusative-case lesson establishes direct objects; this lesson replaces those noun phrases with pronouns.
Requests often use pronouns for people or known objects: 'Ruf ihn an', 'Nimm sie', or 'Hör mir zu' (dative contrast later).

examples.de: Paul ist krank. Ich rufe ihn an.
examples.en: Paul is ill. I am calling him.

examples.de: Das Fenster ist offen. Bitte mach es zu.
examples.en: The window is open. Please close it.

commonMistakes.reason: The accusative form of masculine 'er' is 'ihn'.

specialCases: Feminine 'sie', plural 'sie', and formal 'Sie' are distinguished by context and capitalization.
Some verbs such as 'helfen' take dative rather than accusative: 'Hilf mir'.
Pronoun order with multiple objects is developed at later levels.
tips: Transform full-noun sentences into pronoun sentences.
Drill the three visible changes: mich, dich, ihn.
